discovered-from:SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
data.title: Audit merge gate treats commits on other refs (worklog/backup) as dev integration evidence

Discovered-from: SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ (claim-hold fix).

## Problem
acquireFileLock() (~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts) removes a lock whose acquiredAt is older than DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS (5 min) even when the holder PID is alive on the same host. A long wl sync (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store) therefore has its lock stolen mid-operation, and two writers proceed concurrently: the sync then writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed (the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations).

## Why it was not fixed in SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ
The claim-hold guard now prevents the user-visible damage (a reverted claim), but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Suggested direction
Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative (no age-expiry), keep age-expiry for dead-PID / foreign-host / unparseable locks, and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs. Add a deterministic regression test using the sync-vs-mutation.test.ts git-shim parking technique plus a back-dated lock file.

## Key Files
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts
data.title: wl sync: file-lock age-expiry steals a live holder's lock (residual lost-update hazard)

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (drive timeout reconciliation).

Problem: when implement.py start runs from inside an already-existing worktree (the resume path used by every driven child session), Step 9 writes ImplementState.repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve()) — the worktree path, not the main checkout. phase_finish then calls _remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root) whose safety gate 1 refuses when resolved_path == repo_root (CRITICAL: REFUSE to remove the repository root ... This is the main working tree, not a worktree; Restored status=open).

Impact: every driven child leaks its worktree, finish exits non-zero and restores the item to open even though the commit was pushed — a false failure needing manual status fix; .worklog/worktrees accumulates orphans.

Expected: phase_start should persist the main checkout root (e.g. via _main_checkout_for(worktree) following the gitdir) so phase_finish can remove the worktree after a successful push.

Evidence: SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK finish (commit b11d0877d pushed to dev, finish reported failure, worktree left in place).

Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.
data.title: Standup: separate auto-dispatched from manually dispatched items in 'Yesterday I completed work on...'

# Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner

**Origin:** `discovered-from:OSL-0MVMCP5DT005PIFS` (filed from ContentCreator; that item was deleted once this one existed and was synced).

**Headline:** The framework's v3 pre-push hook refuses every `dev`/`main` push unless the pushed repo ships its own `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, so `install_pi.sh` still ships a gate-less v2 hook to every project without one. Make v3 resolve the runner local-then-global (the pattern the same file already uses for the context-budget gate), ship v3 everywhere, and upgrade stale installed copies.

## Problem statement

Only the SorraAgents checkout contains `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; every other project receives its skills from the global install at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. The v3 hook's full-suite gate looks for the runner at `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only, so in every non-SorraAgents repo the gate hard-fails (`exit 1`) on any push to `dev`/`main`. `scripts/install_pi.sh` works around that by installing `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — a hook **without** the full-suite gate — into every project that lacks a repo-local runner. The result is two hook variants, and the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee is absent from every project except SorraAgents itself.

The cost is visible: `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` had to hand-write a local-then-global runner lookup into ContentCreator's hook (its only deviation from the framework's) before the full-suite push gate could be restored there.

## Users

- **Agents pushing to `dev`** in any framework project — they need the same push-time guarantee everywhere, not only in SorraAgents.
- **The operator / producer** — one hook to audit, one documented contract, no per-repo fork to drift.
- **Project maintainers running `install_pi.sh`** — a fresh install must not choose a weaker hook, and a stale installed hook must not silently keep the weaker one.

Example user stories:

- As an agent pushing to `dev` in a project with no repo-local `skill/` tree, I want the full suite to run through the global runner, so a red tree is refused before it reaches the shared branch.
- As a maintainer, I want `install_pi.sh` to install one hook for every project, so I never have to reason about which variant my repo received.
- As the operator, I want an incomplete install to refuse the push and name the bypass, rather than silently skipping the gate.

## Desired change

1. **Runner resolution (v3 hook).** Resolve the runner local-then-global inside the full-suite gate, mirroring the context-budget block in the same file:
   - `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present;
   - else `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`;
   - when neither exists, fail closed and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (unchanged fail-closed stance, better message).
   This makes the framework hook converge with the block ContentCreator already runs (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` AC2), so the project copy can eventually be deleted rather than forked.
2. **One hook variant.** `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook in every project — the `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` precondition is dropped and `.githooks/pre-push.v2` is removed (or reduced to a pointer note), with the hook-selection comments and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` corrected to describe reality.
3. **Installed-hook upgrade.** `install_pi.sh` must no longer leave a stale installed `.githooks/pre-push` in place forever: when the file's revision marker is a framework revision older than the current one **and the file is an unmodified framework copy**, replace it (backup the previous file, report what happened); when the file carries local modifications, report it and leave it alone. Re-running is idempotent (no rewrite when already current).
4. **Documentation.** The hook contract, the runner resolution order, the revision markers and the upgrade path are documented in the framework docs (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, plus a hook section or `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` mirroring the project-side doc), and the hook header comment states the resolution order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Global runner resolution:** with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` but a global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, a `refs/heads/dev` push through the v3 hook executes the global runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env` from the pushed repo's root, and a green run permits the push (regression test, fake global runner).
- [ ] **Fail-closed unchanged:** with neither runner present, the hook exits non-zero on a `dev`/`main` push and names `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; feature-branch pushes and `refs/worklog/data` pushes still do not invoke the gate.
- [ ] **Parity with the project hook:** the framework gate block and ContentCreator's `.githooks/pre-push` gate block (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX`) resolve the runner identically — same order, same fail-closed message semantics — asserted by a test that compares the two resolution behaviours (not the whole files, because the Worklog-sync ordering still differs).
- [ ] **One variant shipped:** `install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook into a project with no repo-local runner (regression test in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`), and no install path can select a hook without the full-suite gate.

# implement.py parent: terminal blockers still gate topological readiness

discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` builds its dependency graph from **every** in-chain
dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is already terminal, so a
finished blocker still occupies the topological ordering and delays — or in
practice starves — the genuinely ready child that depends on it. A child whose
blockers are all terminal is *ready now*, yet it can be sorted behind unrelated
children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high `sortIndex`.

## Users

- **Primary — agent/operator running an epic:** "As the agent driving an epic
  with `implement.py parent`, I want a child whose blockers are all already
  finished to be selected as soon as it is the lowest-sorting ready child, so
  in-flight implementation work is never skipped and I never have to finish it
  manually."
- **Secondary — producer/reviewer:** "As a producer, I want the reported
  implementation order to mean 'blockers first, then sortIndex', so I can
  predict which child the next run will start."
- **Maintainer:** "As a maintainer, I want the ordering fix covered by a
  regression test with the exact shape that broke, so the readiness rule
  cannot silently regress."

## Observed failure (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

Resolved order for the epic's 8 children:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

`K0V4` (sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound `depends-on`
edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex 8100). `O53Z` was
already `completed`, so `K0V4` should have been ready immediately; instead it
was released only after `O53Z`'s slot near the end of the queue.

Consequences:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4` although its
   worktree held a completed in-flight implementation — it returned
   "start child VDA9"; the in-flight work had to be finished manually with
   `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not "blockers first" in any intuitive sense: a ready
   child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its finished
   blocker sorted late.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Terminal blockers never gate readiness.** In
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` an in-chain dependency edge whose blocker
   is terminal — `_is_terminal_child()` is true: status in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`
   (`in_review`, `completed`, `done`, `deleted`) or the item is soft-deleted —
   contributes neither to `in_degree[child]` nor to `dependents[blocker]`. The
   graph is therefore built over non-terminal children only, and a child whose
   in-chain blockers are all terminal is in the **initial** ready set.
2. **Ready children are ordered by their own `(sortIndex, id)`.** For the
   reproduction shape (open child `LOW` with sortIndex 3000 whose only in-chain
   blocker is a `completed` child `HIGH` with sortIndex 8100, plus an unrelated
   open child `MID` with sortIndex 5000) the resolved order starts with `LOW`,
   then `MID`, then `HIGH` — i.e. `LOW`'s position is decided by its own
   `sortIndex`, never by its blocker's.
3. **Regression test reproduces the exact shape.** A new
   `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` covers at
   minimum: (a) the reproduction shape above, asserting `LOW` is **first**;
   (b) an all-terminal children set, asserting ordering is purely
   `(sortIndex, id)`; (c) a non-terminal chain `A ← B` (both open), asserting
   `A` precedes `B` (real blocking still respected); (d) a soft-deleted blocker
   treated as terminal; (e) an external blocker (id not among the children)
   creating no edge; (f) the existing cycle path still returning
   `([], error)` with the cyclic children named; (g) `_next_child_to_implement`
   still refusing a child whose in-chain blocker is **non**-terminal. The
   reproduction test must be shown red against the pre-fix source and green
   after the fix.
4. **No change to adjacent behaviour.** Cycle detection (fail-fast, no infinite
   recursion), cross-project/external-blocker reporting, `_classify_child`
   (`skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress`) and the blocked-child guard in
   `_next_child_to_implement` are unchanged, and the parent still advances once
   every child is terminal.
5. **Documentation updated.** The
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` docstring states the readiness rule
   (terminal blockers are pre-satisfied), and the parent-recursion/dependency
   ordering text in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (plus any `docs/dev/*` reference
   that describes the ordering) is updated to match; code comments explain why
   terminal edges are excluded.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — the
   implement-skill group (`pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`) is green and the
   full suite (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`) passes on the
   committed tip.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code is agent infrastructure owned by **SorraAgents**:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout contains no `skill/` tree). The item
  was relocated here from the AI_Hell worklog (AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6) by producer
  decision, following the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent, while keeping its
  `discovered-from` link to the AI_Hell epic that exposed the defect. The change,
  its tests, docs, commit and full-suite evidence therefore all stay inside this
  repo — `implement.py start <id>` from this checkout creates the worktree here
  and `wl` resolves this store, so no cross-store resolution is involved.
- **Explicit authorisation to edit `skill/`.** The repository-boundary rule
  forbids editing `skill/` unless explicitly instructed; this work item *is*
  that instruction, scoped to the files listed under **Key Files**.
- **Determinism preserved.** Tie-break stays `(sortIndex, id)`; no
  non-deterministic iteration order (sets are always sorted before use).
- **Narrow scope.** Do **not** change `wl dep` semantics, `sortIndex`
  generation/assignment, child classification, or the `parent` phase's broader
  control flow.
- **No new runtime dependencies;** Python 3.8+ compatible; stdlib only (as the
  existing module is).

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review", "completed", "done", "deleted"}` (~line
  769), `_is_terminal_status()` (~772), `_is_terminal_child()` (~784, also
  treats a soft-deleted `deletedBy` child as terminal).
- `_classify_child()` (~810) — `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`.
- `_resolve_implementation_order(children, blockers)` (~836) — Kahn's
  algorithm; today:

  ```python
  for edge in blockers.get(cid, []):
      bid = str(edge.get("id", ""))
      if bid in child_ids:              # <-- terminal blockers still counted
          in_degree[cid] += 1
          dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  The ready queue is `sorted(... in_degree[cid] == 0 ..., key=(sortIndex, id))`
  and is re-sorted after each release, so a terminal blocker with a high
  `sortIndex` delays its dependent.
- `_next_child_to_implement(children, blockers_map)` (~905) already gates on
  *non-terminal* in-chain blockers (`all(bid in terminal_ids ...)`), so the
  guard and the sort currently disagree — the inconsistency this item fixes.
- Caller `phase_parent` (~5124) calls `_resolve_implementation_order()` and
  returns early on a cycle error; `_next_child_to_implement()` then picks from
  the ordered list.
- Tests live in `skill/implement/tests/` (6 files, `.pi/test-config.json` group
  `implement` → `pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`); **no test currently covers
  `_resolve_implementation_order` or `_next_child_to_implement` directly.**

## Desired change

- Skip terminal blockers when building the graph in
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` — e.g.

  ```python
  if bid in child_ids and not _is_terminal_child(child_by_id[bid]):
      in_degree[cid] += 1
      dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  (equivalently: collapse terminal children out of the graph before the sort).
  Terminal children remain present in the returned order so the caller still
  reports/finishes them, and their own placement is still decided by their own
  `(sortIndex, id)`.
- Cycle detection then operates over the non-terminal subgraph only; keep the
  same error message/format and the fail-fast return.
- Update the docstring (readiness rule + why terminal edges are excluded) and
  the ordering documentation in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Add the regression test module described in AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**:
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` graph construction + docstring;
  `_next_child_to_implement()` docstring cross-reference if needed.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` (SorraAgents) —
  **New**: ordering/readiness regression tests (AC3), including the red-then-
  green reproduction shape.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**: parent-recursion /
  dependency-order text states that terminal blockers do not gate readiness.
- `docs/dev/*` in SorraAgents — **Edit (if present)**: any ordering description
  that contradicts the new rule (verify with
  `grep -rn "topological\|dependency order" docs/ skill/implement/`).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Masking a real cycle.* Excluding terminal blockers from the graph could hide
  a cycle that passes through a terminal child. Mitigation: a cycle can only
  block work that still needs doing, so detection over the non-terminal
  subgraph is the correct semantics; document it in the docstring and cover it
  with AC3(f) (cycle among non-terminal children still fails fast).
- *Accidental behaviour drift elsewhere.* `_next_child_to_implement()` has its
  own terminal-aware guard; the fix must align with it rather than replace it.
  Mitigation: AC3(g) asserts the guard still refuses non-terminal-blocked
  children; AC4 forbids changing adjacent paths.
- *Cross-repo verification gap.* The AI_Hell audit/CI cannot see SorraAgents
  files, so a green AI_Hell report does not prove the fix. Mitigation: run the
  implement-skill pytest group and the SorraAgents full suite from the
  SorraAgents worktree and record the evidence (red/green, commit hash) on this
  item, per AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- *Test-gate selection.* Changed-scope selection may not see the new test file
  until it is tracked; Mitigation: `git add` before the gate run and confirm the
  `implement` group is selected (otherwise fall back to full scope).
- *Scope creep.* The 2026-10-23 report also notes the confusing reported order
  generally and the manual `finish K0V4` step; richer ordering diagnostics or
  `parent`-phase rework are **not** in scope. Mitigation: record follow-ups as
  separate items (see Related work) rather than widening this fix.

**Assumptions**

- The item now lives in the **SorraAgents** worklog (relocated from AI_Hell by
  producer decision, per the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent); the AI_Hell epic
  AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S remains recorded as the origin via `discovered-from`.
- Terminal blockers are pre-satisfied for *ordering* purposes but are still
  reported in the resolved order (existing `skip-terminal` classification
  handles them in the loop), so no caller contract changes.
- Soft-deleted children behave as terminal for this rule (they can never be
  implemented) — consistent with `_is_terminal_child()`.

### Goal

Extend the in-repo, fail-open Herdr CLI helper with a session-level pane/agent
boundary and provide a deterministic recording **fake** Herdr CLI, so the pane
transport and its tests can exercise `pane split` / `agent start` /
`agent prompt` / `agent wait` / `pane close` without a live Herdr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive runs `pane split` (no `tab create`/`workspace create`) with `--cwd`, started via `agent start` and prompted via `agent prompt --wait`; asserted by a fake-CLI test.
- A recording fake Herdr CLI (test-only shim plus in-process runner with scripted responses) lets tests assert exact herdr invocations (arguments and order) and simulate `done`, `blocked`, `timeout`, `agent_not_ready` and CLI-failure transitions with no live Herdr.
- Agent names `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` are validated against herdr's `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` rule with deterministic truncation; unit tests cover valid, truncated and collision cases.
- `agent start` requiring an interactive shell prompt is handled: `agent_not_ready` is retried within the configured wait budget or surfaced as a reported reason — never a crash.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- **Forked-decision resolution (intake Appendix):** keep the boundary in
  `skill/shared/` and reuse `herdr_pane.py`'s `HERDR_BIN_PATH` resolution,
  subprocess env handling and fail-open return style — do not duplicate that
  logic. Additive changes only to in-repo files; no edits to repo-external
  herdr skill or `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.
- Surface (one injectable client, every call returning a parsed result or a
  fail-open `{"success": false, "reason": ...}`, never raising):
  `pane split --current --cwd <path> [--env K=V] [--focus|--no-focus]`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve --no-extensions`,
  `agent prompt <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`,
  `agent wait <name> --until done|blocked`, `pane close <id>`,
  `pane rename <id> <label>`.
- Parse ids defensively from `.result.pane.pane_id` and agent JSON; treat
  unknown shapes as a reported failure (Herdr API-drift mitigation).
- Fake CLI lives under the tests tree (`skill/shared/tests/`), scripted by the
  test, emitting JSON matching the real CLI shape.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`
- `skill/shared/herdr_session.py` (new, if split out)
- `skill/shared/tests/fake_herdr_cli.py` (new)

None — foundation slice; blocks the spawner and lifecycle slices.

  rename) reusing `herdr_pane.py` conventions.
- Recording fake Herdr CLI + fixtures.
- Unit tests, all green, no live Herdr needed.
- Short reference-doc note for the helper.

Add `_pane_session_spawner` next to `_default_session_spawner` and select the
transport per invocation: pane driving only when Herdr is detected **and** the
operator opted in; otherwise the existing headless `pi -p` spawner is used

### Goal

Drive the pane-side lifecycle to completion in `phase_drive`: wait on session
state (never process exit), report blocked children, bound the wait with the
existing timeouts, and close or explicitly retain every pane — with additive
report parity for human and `--json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child is decided by `agent wait --until done|blocked` plus the `phase_parent` stage re-read; tests cover done, blocked, timeout.
- **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent reports `blocked`, drive stops, records `blocked_child`/`blocked_pane`, leaves the pane open and names it.
- **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once its child reaches a terminal stage or (b) retained and reported; tests assert close per success and no close when blocked.
- **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` and `--max-child-sessions` still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane and stops the chain.
- **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport`; the summary lists retained panes, asserted by tests.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `phase_parent` stays the authority for terminality; the `agent wait` result
  is only a fast-path/stop signal. Reuse `_reconcile_spawn_failure` so a child
  that reached a terminal stage before the wait expired is still reported as
  `completed-late`, not failed.
- `blocked` → report keys `blocked_child` / `blocked_pane`, a `retained_panes`
  entry, and an actionable message naming the pane (e.g.
  `herdr pane read <pane_id>`); title the pane via
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` (`⚠️`/`🚫` verdicts).
- Close path: `pane close <id>` after the child's terminal stage is confirmed;
  retain on blocked/failed with a verdict title. Never leak silently.
- `_emit_phase_report` gains additive keys only; the human rendering appends a
  "panes retained for inspection" list. Existing deterministic orchestration
  tests (`ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`) keep passing unchanged.
- Timeout behaviour keeps today's semantics: close the pane, record `reason`,
  stop the chain (reconciled against the child's real stage first).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_drive`, `_emit_phase_report`)
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

## Dependencies

- Pane session spawner and opt-in transport selection.

## Deliverables

- done / blocked / timeout lifecycle handling with `phase_parent` authority.
- Close-or-retain rule with pane-title verdicts.
- Report fields (`pane_id`, `transport`, blocked/retained panes) plus human
  rendering, with parity tests.
- Doc updates for blocked-child handling and retained panes.

## Goal

Replace the whole-directory `node_modules` symlink in `implement.py start` with a **worktree-local link farm** so workspace packages resolve to the worktree's own source tree. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1695 in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main-checkout>/node_modules`. ## Goal

Make `implement.py finish` **fail closed** when a worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — an actionable error naming the stale path and remediation, so a green gate never silently passes on the wrong code. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`phase_finish` runs build → test gate → commit from the worktree. If resolution is stale (worktree's `@worklog/shared` → main checkout's `packages/shared/dist`), the gate either false-reds on correct new code (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) or false-greens on broken code. The gate currently cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from "shared code unchanged" and exposes no resolution diagnostic.

## Desired change (producer-decided: hard-fail)

## Problem

During the `implement.py finish` refactor step for **SA-0MVO58B4J004Y40C**, pre-existing smells discovered in files that were only *merged* in from `origin/dev` were annotated by prepending a REFACTOR marker block at byte 0 of the file:

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — marker block (lines 1-5) now precedes `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, so the shebang is no longer the first line of the file.
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — marker block prepended (harmless: no shebang, and comments do not disturb the module docstring).

## Root cause

`inject_refactor_comment()` in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` unconditionally writes `comment_block + original_content`:

```python
new_content = comment_block + original_content
```

The marker block therefore lands at byte 0 even when line 1 of the file is an interpreter directive (`#!`). `_build_comment_block()` additionally prefixes the block with `"
"`, so a blank line is inserted between the marker and the shebang, and the shebang ends up on line 6.

## Goal

Injecting a REFACTOR marker must never displace an interpreter directive: a file that starts with a shebang keeps that shebang on line 1, so the file keeps a valid interpreter line for direct execution and shebang-parsing tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Injecting into a file whose first line is a shebang places the REFACTOR block after that shebang line; line 1 of the file remains byte-identical to the original shebang.
- Injecting into a file with no shebang keeps the current placement: the REFACTOR block is added above the first code line.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` again starts with `#!/usr/bin/env python3` on line 1, and its existing `REFACTOR-SA-0MVPTU74Y005WAY0` marker is preserved immediately below it (tracking is not dropped).
- `has_existing_comment()` still reports `True` for the smell type of a marker that now sits below a shebang, so re-injection stays idempotent.
- Regression tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a Python file with a shebang, a non-Python style file with a shebang (e.g. `.sh`), and a file without a shebang (unchanged placement); all existing tests in that module continue to pass.

## Scope notes

- Not in scope: making `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` executable. It is currently mode `664`, and the missing executable bit is a separate ruff `EXE001` smell tracked by **SA-0MVPTU74Y005WAY0**.
- Not in scope: removing stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes (**SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9**).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`

## Open Questions

- OPEN QUESTION (to the implementer): should the insertion point also step past a Python encoding cookie (`# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-`), which PEP 263 requires within the first two lines? A file with both a shebang and a cookie would still push the cookie to line 3+ after this fix. Recording only — do not expand scope without confirmation.

## Problem

A full-project  run reports fixes that were never applied.

Observed on 2026-10-28 (SorraAgents @ dev):
- Report claimed `Auto-fixed: 8`, listing EXE005, ISC004, PLW1510 and RUF059 findings.
- `git status` afterwards showed **no source changes at all** (only the unrelated `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` scheduled-prompt timestamp).

Verified cause: those diagnostics are *not* auto-fixable (`ruff check --fix` reports `fix: null` for EXE005/PLW1510/RUF059 and `fix.applicability: unsafe` for ISC004).

## Root cause

`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output` (line ~113) converts **every** diagnostic in ruff's JSON output into a `fixed_findings` entry, without inspecting `item['fix']` or `item['fix']['applicability']`. `auto_fix_files` (line ~217) then sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0` and the report prints those as auto-fixes. Ruff emits all diagnostics (fixed and unfixed) in its JSON output, so the count is the number of *diagnostics seen*, not fixes applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output` has the same shape (counts every message; eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields are ignored).

## Expected behaviour

- Only count a finding as auto-fixed when the linter actually applied an edit: ruff `item['fix']` is not `None` **and** `fix.applicability == 'safe'` (the default for `--fix` without `--unsafe-fixes`).
- Unfixable/unsafe diagnostics should either be dropped or surfaced as *remaining* smells, so they still reach smell detection, REFACTOR comments and work items.
- `fixes_applied`, the summary's `auto_fixed` count and the human-readable report must agree with what actually changed on disk.
- Add a regression test: a file with only-unsafe / no-fix diagnostics must report `Auto-fixed: 0`, and a file with a safe fix must report `Auto-fixed: 1` and be changed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output` only records findings whose fix is present and safe.
2. A full-project run against a tree whose only diagnostics are unsafe/unfixable reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A tree with one safe fix reports `Auto-fixed: 1` and the file is modified on disk.
4. Unsafe/unfixable diagnostics are still represented in the `Remaining smells` section (or equivalent) rather than silently dropped.
5. New unit tests in `skill/refactor/tests/` cover both cases.
6. Existing `skill/refactor` tests pass.

## Notes

Discovered from the `/skill:refactor` full-scan scheduled run. The 8 flagged diagnostics are already tracked by open REFACTOR items (SA-0MVRCL0Q90016C7D, SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW, SA-0MVRBPY7J004GJAI, SA-0MVPTU9HG00146UV), so this item is only about report/labelling accuracy.
data.title: refactor skill reports false auto-fixes for unfixable linter diagnostics

# implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps

`discovered-from:SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` — split out of the driven-session worktree-removal fix at producer request (Q2 of that item's intake). Same root cause, different caller: here the *session that invoked finish* is the operator's own agent session, not a driver-spawned child.

**Headline:** `implement.py finish` must not leave a plain leaf session unable to run any command: after finish removes the worktree, Pi's bash tool refuses every call in that session, so the report, the worklog comment and the post-push verification steps all fail.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` removes the worktree after the dev push (Step 7, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:5322`). In the plain leaf flow the finishing process is a **child** of the agent session (`bash` tool), and that session's cwd *is* the worktree. `_remove_worktree` chdirs only the finish process out of the tree (`:2364-2376`), so the session keeps a deleted cwd: Pi's bash tool then rejects every command with `Working directory does not exist: … / Cannot execute bash commands.` while absolute-path `read`/`write` still work. The session is reduced to a degraded loop exactly when it should be writing its completion comment, rendering its report and verifying the pushed commit.

## Users and user stories

- **Implement agent (plain leaf item)** — "As an agent finishing a leaf work item, I want my post-finish steps to run normally, so I do not have to invent absolute-path workarounds for the report and the post-push verification."
- **Operator / reviewer** — "As the reviewer, I want the session's final report and verification evidence produced by the workflow rather than improvised, so I can trust what I read."
- **Maintainer** — "As the maintainer, I want one deterministic rule for when a worktree may be deleted relative to the session that owns it."

## Recorded evidence

- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** (session `01a1840b-13a6-71a0-9153-f89e8dd2dfee`, TCE repo): the session hit `Working directory does not exist` **8 times** after its foreground `implement.py finish`, then worked around it — its own transcript notes "After that bash won't work, so do it last", and it removed a placeholder directory as its final action.
- Same failure mode documented in `SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` for driven sessions (where it also wedges the drive loop); that item fixes the driven case only.

## Desired change (direction, not a fixed design)

The driven case is solved by deferring removal to the driver. The plain case has no external owner, so the options are:

1. **Defer to the session's own last step** — finish keeps the worktree and the implement skill's finish step ends with an explicit, runnable cleanup instruction (`git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`) that the *session* performs as its final action, after the comment, report and verification are done.
2. **Defer to a separate cleanup pass** — finish always defers; the cleanup skill / `implement.py` gains a `cleanup` action that removes worktrees of terminal items, run by the operator or the next workflow step.
3. **Make finish's removal non-fatal to the session** — keep removing, but ensure nothing after it needs bash (move report rendering/comment/verification *before* removal inside finish). Cheapest, but leaves the session's cwd dead for any later operator-driven interaction.

A design decision is required at intake/plan time; option 1 or 2 is expected to fit the existing `--keep-worktree` hatch added by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report.
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path.
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (finish step cleanup instructions), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` state the ownership rule for the plain flow.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`), and the dev-push full-suite gate is green for the pushed commit.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the driven-session behaviour delivered by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR; this item is the non-driven path only.
- Reuse `_remove_worktree`, `cleanup_worktree_processes` and the existing safety gates; no new deletion mechanism, no `rm -rf`-style shortcuts.
- Never remove a worktree that is dirty or whose item is non-terminal.
- Pi core's bash-tool behaviour on a missing cwd is out of scope (a Pi-core limitation, not fixable here).
- **Out of scope:** the pane transport, `hygiene_check.sh` rework, branch deletion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 6b/7 and the finish-step ordering, plus the deferral predicate shared with SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish-step cleanup instructions (currently a manual `git worktree remove` block, `SKILL.md:811`).
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend the finish test harness (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py` style) for the plain-flow behaviour.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — ownership rule for the plain flow.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it" (open, parent of this split): fixes the driven path; this item must reuse its deferral mechanism.
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** — finish SIGTERMing itself in `wl cleanup-worktree` (completed): the self-exclusion contract around Step 6b.
- **SA-0MRTSO5W8005ZGA7** — added the worktree process cleanup call to the workflow (completed).
- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** — the plain-flow session that hit the deleted cwd 8 times (completed).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Options 1/2 leave worktrees behind on interruption** — mitigated by AC4 and by the cleanup skill.
- **Doc/instruction drift:** `SKILL.md` currently instructs the agent to run `git worktree remove` itself after pushing, duplicating finish's removal; the chosen option must make the instruction and the code agree.
- **Assumption:** the operator's session is the only other holder of the worktree cwd in the plain flow (no other process needs it), so removal timing is purely about the session's own remaining steps.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "just make Pi tolerate a deleted cwd" is a Pi-core change — record it, do not attempt it here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope split.** *Answer (producer, during SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR intake): "driver only, raise a follow up item for the plain leaf flow".* This item is that follow-up; the driven path is SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION, for planning) — Which cleanup owner for the plain flow?** (1) the session's own final step, (2) a separate cleanup pass, (3) move everything that needs bash before removal inside finish. Recommended: **(1)**, because it keeps a single workflow run responsible for its own cleanup and reuses the `--keep-worktree` hatch; (2) becomes preferable if the cleanup skill is the operator's normal sweep.
- **Q3 (answered by research) — Is the failure a hang?** No: bash is refused for the rest of the session while absolute-path file tools still work; the session degrades but does not block (RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33's workaround).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** – implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it (in-progress)
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** – implement.py finish SIGTERMs itself in wl cleanup-worktree, stranding the dev push (completed)
- **SA-0MVMMHG9Z004F2ED** – implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+267 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+253 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvjc5knt0044l2b, absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+246 more)

# plan/intake AC coverage review creates duplicate "Close coverage gap" children when covering children already exist

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — observed while running `/skill:plan`.

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py:apply_coverage_review` (`action: auto_close`) creates one child per *parent AC it judges uncovered*, with the AC text copied verbatim and the title `Close coverage gap: [ ] **ACn — …**`. On a parent whose six feature children each restate an AC in their own words, it judged **all five** ACs uncovered and created five thin `idea`-stage duplicates alongside the real children.

Observed on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`:

- Six properly-formed children existed (config+guard, docs, three AC-verification children, validation) before the review ran.
- `apply_coverage_review(..., target_stage='plan_complete')` returned `action: auto_close` and created `MS-0MVTEXGU6007Z48U`, `MS-0MVTEXH6F008DVJF`, `MS-0MVTEXHK8002E376`, `MS-0MVTEXHWT0074M3M`, `MS-0MVTEXI9G002ROD0` (AC1–AC5).
- A follow-up `run_coverage_review` then reported `coverage_pct: 100` — mapping each parent AC **only** to the newly created gap child, i.e. the review's own output became its evidence.
- Resolution taken: all five were closed as duplicates with a comment mapping each AC to its real covering child, and the parent recorded the outcome.

## Why it matters

- The review silently degrades a well-planned tree (6 children) into 11, half of them AC-text stubs with no key files, constraints or evidence requirement — the opposite of what the review is meant to enforce.
- The "coverage" metric measures lexical similarity between the parent AC text and child AC text, not whether the child actually discharges the AC, so a correctly reworded child scores as a gap.
- Closing the duplicates afterwards leaves the parent at `plan_complete` with the tool's mapping invalidated, so a later re-run is ambiguous (re-create the stubs, or report gaps?).

## Suggested direction

- Before creating a gap child, require a **semantic/structural** match — e.g. child AC coverage by the parent's AC identifier (`AC1`, `AC2`, …, tolerant of reworded text) or by an explicit `Covers: ACn` line in the child description — and skip creation when matched.
- Treat `parent AC -> child` mapping as evidence only when the child has a non-stub body (ACs + Key Files/evidence), and prefer reporting `stop` with the specific unmatched ACs over creating thin children.
- Make the post-`auto_close` mapping exclude the auto-created children themselves when reporting `coverage_pct` (no self-satisfying evidence).
- Cover the case with a test: parent with 5 ACs, 5 reworded covering children → `action: proceed`, no children created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parent whose ACs are all covered by existing children — including children that reword the AC text — yields `action: proceed` and creates **zero** children.
- [ ] Gap children are created only when no child declares or demonstrably discharges the AC; the created child still restates the AC verbatim (current behaviour preserved for genuine gaps).
- [ ] `coverage_pct` never counts a gap child created by the same review as coverage for its own AC.
- [ ] Unit test(s) cover: fully-covered-with-reworded-AC → proceed; genuinely uncovered AC → auto_close with exactly one child; idempotent re-run creates no duplicates.
- [ ] `plan`/`intake` SKILL.md text states how coverage is matched, so agents can declare coverage (`Covers: ACn`) instead of relying on wording.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `run_coverage_review`, `apply_coverage_review`, AC extraction/matching.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — the documented coverage step.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tests/` — coverage-review unit tests.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — the planning session where this was observed (children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W`, `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA`, `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`).

# implement.py finish must push from the tree it is pushing (dev-push gate validates the pushed commit)

## Problem statement

The dev-push full-suite gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) verifies the tree of the
**directory the push was launched from** (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` →
`run_tests.py --project-root`), not the tree of the commit being pushed.
`implement.py finish` normally keeps those in step by fast-forwarding the main
checkout to the new commit before pushing from the main checkout — but the
non-fast-forward retry path breaks the invariant: `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`
rebases **inside the worktree** (rewriting the commit) and then retries
`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)` from the main checkout, which still holds the
pre-rebase commit. The gate therefore verifies the pre-rebase commit's tree and
can serve its cached full-suite entry, while the rebased commit lands on `dev`
never having been gated.

Because the cache key is `HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash + suite command
(`skill/test_cache.py::compute_git_state` / `cache_key`), the wrong-tree run is
not a random collision: it deterministically verifies a *different commit* and
records green evidence for it.

## Users

- **AI agents running `/skill:implement`** — rely on "the dev push succeeded"
  meaning "the full suite ran against what landed".
- **Producers / release operators** — rely on the invariant *landed on `dev`
  ⇒ full suite green at that commit* when approving a finish or a release.
- **Auditors / reviewers** — rely on the cached full-suite entry at the pushed
  commit as evidence (`run_tests.py --summary`, audit F3).

Example user stories:

- "As an agent whose `dev` push was rejected non-fast-forward, when the finish
  rebases and retries, I expect the full suite to have run against the rebased
  commit."
- "As a producer, I expect a finish to fail loudly rather than push a commit
  the gate never verified."

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Push cwd is the pushed tree.** `implement.py finish` runs its dev push
   from the checkout that has the pushed commit checked out (the worktree) —
   for the first attempt *and* the non-fast-forward retry — or otherwise passes
   the pushed tree explicitly to the gate. The main checkout's working tree is
   never the subject of the dev-push gate.
2. **Retry path re-establishes the subject.** After the recovery rebase
   rewrites the commit, the retry push has the rebased commit checked out, so
   the hook's `--project-root` is the pushed tree. If that tree cannot be
   materialised (worktree gone, dirty in a way that cannot be rebased), the
   finish **fails closed** with an actionable message naming the commit,
   branch and worktree — it never silently pushes from a checkout holding a
   different commit.
3. **Gate evidence is surfaced.** Hook/push `stderr` is logged by
   `git_push_to_dev()` on success too (at least INFO/DEBUG), and the gate's
   resolved tree is visible in that output (root path, `HEAD` sha, pushed sha,
   executed-vs-cached), so "the gate ran and hit a cache for commit X" is
   distinguishable from "the gate never ran".
4. **Regression tests.** An automated test asserts the retry push's cwd/root is
   the worktree (unit test around `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` /
   `git_push_to_dev`), plus a test that a `HEAD` ≠ pushed-sha mismatch cannot
   silently gate the wrong tree (it is either corrected or refused). No
   wall-clock timing proxies.
5. **Rollout to every project that needs the change.** Refresh the machine-wide
   skill install from SorraAgents (`scripts/install_pi.sh`) and verify the
   installed copy carries the change; update each consuming project's
   documentation that asserts the old behaviour (at minimum
   `llm/docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and this repo's `docs/dev/*`), and record in
   this work item the verified list of projects/checkouts (all project clones
   inherit the fix through the global skill install; project copies of
   `.githooks/pre-push` are unaffected unless the hook itself changes).
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Cache compatibility.** Full-suite evidence is keyed by suite command + git
  state (`HEAD` sha + content hash of dirty paths) and is **path-independent**,
  so pushing from the worktree keeps reusing existing entries and keeps writing
  audit-acceptable entries (`scope: full`). Any change must preserve this.
- **Other gates must keep working from a worktree push:** branch policy,
  context-budget gate (it must measure the pushed tree — the worktree), worklog
  sync (already skipped for linked worktrees), and `mirror_suite_cache`
  (already mirrors a worktree's private test cache into the main checkout's
  `.worklog/cache`).
- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends stay explicit escape
  hatches; the default path must never fail open.
- **Preserve existing recovery behaviour:** push timeout → process-group kill +
  recoverable-state comment; non-fast-forward → fetch + rebase + retry;
  worktree retained until the push succeeds.
- **Repo boundary.** The change lands here (SorraAgents). The reporting item
  `LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3` (llm) owns no code; it is a cross-reference only.
- **Scope discipline.** Gate-side hardening (making the hook itself detect a
  `HEAD` ≠ pushed-sha mismatch) is *out of scope* for this item: the producer
  chose the pusher-side fix. If the gate-side safety net is wanted later, it
  becomes its own item (see Related work).

## Existing state

- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new
  commit (`LOG.info("Fast-forward to %s succeeded")`), Step 6 pushes from
  `repo_root` (main checkout, `implement.py:5235`), and on
  `PushNonFastForwardError` calls `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`, which
  fetches, rebases in the worktree, then retries `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`
  (`implement.py:4737`). Nothing re-points the main checkout at the rebased
  commit (`_sync_parent_branch` runs only after a successful push).
- `git_push_to_dev()` captures hook output with `subprocess.PIPE` and logs
  `stderr` **only on failure**.
- `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"` and
  already has `mirror_suite_cache` for worktree pushes — the hook was written
  expecting pushes from linked worktrees.
- Observed 2026-10-28 (`LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0`): finish took ~68 s end to end
  (commit → nff rejection → rebase → success) and no cache entry existed for
  the pushed tree; git runs the pre-push hook *before* contacting the remote,
  so neither push appears to have executed the suite. Unexplained by the
  wrong-tree defect alone; AC3's evidence surfacing is the way to make it
  diagnosable.

## Desired change

- Push from the worktree (the checkout holding the pushed commit) on both the
  first attempt and the retry, so the hook's resolved `--project-root` is the
  pushed tree; keep the Step-5 fast-forward only as a main-checkout hygiene
  step (or drop it if it becomes redundant) without making it the gate subject.
- Fail closed with an actionable message when the pushed commit cannot be
  checked out for the push.
- Log the push/hook output on success, including the gate's resolved tree
  evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Step 6 push cwd (currently
  `repo_root`), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` retry push cwd,
  `git_push_to_dev()` stderr logging on success, fail-closed path.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — new retry-path/cwd regression test (alongside
  `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document that the dev push runs from the
  worktree so the gate validates the pushed commit.
- `docs/dev/*` (this repo) and `~/projects/llm/docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — state
  that the gate's subject is the pushed commit and how evidence is surfaced.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3** (llm worklog) — the investigation that produced this
  item; now a cross-reference only. Full root-cause evidence, the corrected
  cache-key analysis and the original observed timeline live there.
- **LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9** (llm worklog) — same class of defect via a different
  trigger: the Step-5 fast-forward is *skipped* when the main checkout is
  dirty, so the gate verifies a stale main checkout. The pusher-side fix here
  (push from the worktree) also removes that trigger; whoever implements this
  should review that item's ACs and close it if satisfied.
- **LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK** — activated `.githooks/pre-push` (`core.hooksPath`),
  the gate this item makes trustworthy.
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** — earlier period where the gate did not run at all
  (`core.hooksPath` unset); explains some historic "no gate" observations.
- **SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY** — concurrent finishes orphaning commits via the
  shared local-dev fast-forward (adjacent main-checkout mutation surface).
- **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — finish reports push failure when the push actually
  landed (adjacent push-result reporting).
- Docs/code: `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`,
  `skill/test_cache.py` (cache-key semantics), `.githooks/pre-push`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (verified):** cache keys are path-independent, so pushing from
  the worktree reuses/creates the same audit-accepted entries as a main-checkout
  push at that commit. Mitigation: assert in a test.
- **Risk:** pushing from a worktree changes the hook's context-budget gate
  subject (worktree instead of main checkout). It should be *more* correct
  (the pushed files), but thresholds are read from the pushed tree — verify the
  gate still passes for a normal finish.
- **Risk:** worktree removal ordering — the push must keep happening before
  `git worktree remove` (already the case; a retry needs the worktree).
- **Risk:** a fail-closed retry blocks a finish that previously "succeeded"
  (silently ungated). Intended, but the message must name the manual remedy.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "gate the pushed commit" invites rewriting the hook
  as well. Gate-side hardening is explicitly out of scope here; record it as a
  follow-up item if the producer wants the safety net.
- **Assumption:** the 2026-10-28 68-second anomaly is not reproducible as a
  unit test; AC3 instrumentation is the intended diagnosis path.

---

## Plan (2026-10-30, /skill:plan)

Effort **Small** / risk **Medium** → planning required (pre-check `decision: plan`);
approval gate `request_approval: false` (not Extra Large + High/Severe), so the
plan proceeded straight to the automated review stages.

Five vertical slices, test-first (children in dependency order):

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | Regression tests pin the dev-push gate subject (SA-0MVUTXILY003DVTE) | task | — | 4 |
| 2 | Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN) | bug | 1 | 1, 2 |
| 3 | Surface dev-push gate evidence on success (SA-0MVUTXJM8006PQY4) | feature | 2 | 3 |
| 4 | Document the worktree push and gate evidence (SA-0MVUTXK41000FC08) | docs | 2, 3 | 6 |
| 5 | Verify rollout and reconcile overlapping gate items (SA-0MVUTXKKP0005DWS) | chore | 4 | 5, 7 |

### Design decisions carried into the children

- **Push cwd = worktree on both attempts.** Step 6 pushes from `worktree_path`
  (the checkout holding the pushed commit); `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`
  recomputes the rebased commit from the worktree and retries from there. The
  Step-5 local-dev fast-forward and the main-checkout guard stay on
  `repo_root` as hygiene only — never the gate subject.
- **Fail closed.** A new pre-push subject guard asserts the push cwd's `HEAD`
  equals the pushed sha and raises an error naming commit, branch, worktree and
  actual `HEAD` instead of pushing from a checkout holding a different commit.
- **Evidence without touching project hooks.** Gate evidence (root, `HEAD`,
  pushed sha, executed-vs-cached) is emitted pusher-side from the read-only
  test-cache API, because per-project `.githooks/pre-push` copies are
  per-project files that would need manual propagation, while the pusher-side
  change reaches every project through `~/.pi/agent/skills` →
  `SorraAgents/skill` (the rollout mechanism AC5 relies on). Hook-side evidence
  is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION (Q5) if the producer wants it later.
- **Cache compatibility preserved.** Cache keys stay path-independent
  (`HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash + suite command), so worktree pushes reuse
  and create the same audit-acceptable `scope: full` entries;
  `mirror_suite_cache` is unchanged.

### Automated review stages (completed; conservative changes only)

1. Requirements & AC alignment — all seven parent ACs trace to exactly one
   child; no invented ACs; AC3/AC5/AC6 child wording aligned to the parent
   phrasing so coverage is explicit.
2. Completeness — every child has goal, ACs, Key Files (validated with
   `validate_key_files_format()` → no issues), minimal implementation,
   definition of done and dependencies.
3. Sequencing & dependencies — test slice first; evidence before docs; docs
   before rollout; no cycles.
4. Scope sizing — five deliverable increments; the test/fix split is kept
   deliberately to preserve test-first ordering.
5. Acceptance & testability — every AC is pass/fail with a named artefact;
   no wall-clock timing proxies (the executed-vs-cached classification is driven
   by staged cache entries).
6. Polish & handoff — copy-pasteable steps, file paths verified against the
   working tree, cross-repo path correction recorded (Q6).

AC coverage review: `proceed` — 100 % of parent ACs covered by children
(`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`).

### Plan changelog

- 2026-10-30 — initial decomposition (5 children, 7 dependency edges) created;
  duplicate-work check performed against `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3`,
  `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH`, `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` (see Q7).

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — where should the fix land?** — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29,
  interactive reply): **option (b), pusher-side only.** A SorraAgents (`SA-`)
  item changes `implement.py` to push from the worktree and surface hook
  stderr; the `LP-` investigation item becomes a report/cross-reference and
  closes. Additional instruction: *"ensure the work item there has an AC of
  updating all projects that need it"* → recorded as AC5 (rollout to every
  project that needs the change, with the verified list recorded here).
  Prior recommendation (advisory, not chosen): option (c), both halves.
- **Q2 — gate behaviour when the push cwd's `HEAD` is not the pushed commit?**
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29, interactive reply): **option (c)** — gate the
  pushed commit transparently when the tree can be materialised, fail closed
  otherwise. Recorded as AC1 (push from the tree holding the commit) plus AC2's
  fail-closed clause.
  Prior recommendation (advisory, matches the answer): option (c).
- **Q3 (resolved during intake) — relationship to `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9`?**
  Partial overlap only (different trigger: skipped fast-forward vs rebase
  retry); both are addressed by this item's pusher-side fix. Evidence: both
  descriptions plus the `implement.py` Step-5/Step-6/`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  code paths.
- **Q4 (resolved during intake) — is the test-cache key path-dependent?** No:
  `compute_git_state` hashes `HEAD` + dirty-path content and `cache_key` adds
  the suite command; `--project-root` is not part of the key. Evidence: source
  read of `skill/test_cache.py` and the cache-query call sites in
  `run_tests.py` / `audit_runner.py`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** – Implement skill safety gate should account for git worktrees (completed)

# Plain-flow finish deferral: keep the worktree, report it loudly, prove it with tests

Parent: **SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5** — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps*.

**Goal.** In the plain leaf flow the worktree must still exist when `implement.py finish` returns, and finish must say so loudly enough that the session always runs the follow-up cleanup.

## Context

The deferral mechanism itself is delivered by **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` for driven children, plus the explicit `finish --keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE=1` hatch). This child is the **non-driven half**: it pins the plain-leaf behaviour with tests, closes any plain-flow gap the sibling leaves (e.g. a deferral report field written only on the driven path), and adds the "retained worktree" surface that makes a forgotten cleanup self-healing.

Root cause (parent): `phase_finish` Step 7 removes the worktree while the *session* still has its cwd inside it; Pi's bash tool then refuses every command (`Working directory does not exist`), while absolute-path `read`/`write` keep working — the session degrades exactly when it must write its comment, render its report and verify the pushed commit (evidence: **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33**).

Constraints inherited from the parent and the sibling item:

- **Do not change the driven behaviour.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` semantics, driver-side removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as the sibling item delivers them; existing driven tests must stay green.
- **No third removal path and no new predicate.** `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE` (and `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`) are the only deferral inputs; removal itself stays `_remove_worktree` + `cleanup_worktree_processes`.
- **Deferral must not be silent**: report field, log line and a copy-pasteable follow-up command.
- **Nothing after Step 7 needs the worktree** (verified in the sibling item's research: parent-branch sync, terminal-status write/read-back and the completion comment all act on the main checkout), so deferring cannot break the rest of finish.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state: with boundaries patched and the session cwd inside the worktree, the worktree and `.implement_state.json` still exist after finish returns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report: `steps.worktree_removal == {"deferred": true, "reason": ..., "path": ...}`, the human and JSON output name the retained path with the exact `implement.py cleanup <work-item-id>` follow-up command (also added to the completion comment), and finish still reaches its terminal state (`completed` / `in_review`, push landed, status read-back passes).
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path: no new environment variable and no `/proc`-based holder detection, and without those flags `phase_finish` still runs `cleanup_worktree_processes` + `_remove_worktree`, reporting `worktree_removed: true` (the regression pin that keeps the sibling item's AC2 assertions green).
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent: re-running `phase_finish` on a retained worktree duplicates no state, `phase_start` resumes on the retained worktree instead of failing on `git worktree add`, and a subsequent `implement.py cleanup <id>` (child 1) removes it.
- [ ] **Driven behaviour untouched.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` semantics, driver-side removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR delivers them; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`); tests are written first (TDD).

## Minimal implementation

1. Pin the contract in a new `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_plain_flow_keep_worktree.py` (patched-boundary harness modelled on `test_finish_no_diff_status.py`).
2. Close any plain-flow gap in `phase_finish`: deferral report field + loud retained-path output/comment for the `--keep-worktree` path (the sibling owns the driven path).
3. Assert idempotence and `phase_start` resume-on-retained-worktree behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_plain_flow_keep_worktree.py` — new tests.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` (deferral report surface + retained-path output), `phase_start` (resume path, verification only).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — patterns to follow and regressions to keep green.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — the `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE` hatch and the deferral predicate must exist before this item's tests can assert them.
